tools.name: make_cartoon
tools.description: The quickest way to a cartoon: send the script as people write one, a line each, Name: what they say, and get the jabbertoon.com link that opens it in the editor ready to play and to record as a video (free, no account). Read too: (happy, waves) in a line; [Leo walks to Mia] on a line of its own; Pl

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Call this first, except for make_cartoon. One topic of Jabbertoon's guide as Markdown (under 20,000 characters): start (what it makes and the order of calls), cartoon (the JSON program: cast, scenes, lines, moves), text (the same cartoon as screenplay text), moves, characters, voices, places, errors

tools.name: list_moves
tools.description: Lists the ready-made moves a character can do (walk in, wave hello, hop, bow, slump, talk...): id, name, length in seconds, the bodies it works on (two legs, four, none), its settings with units, page and links. A does block plays one: {"op": "does", "who": "dog", "behaviour": "c4c:beh:wave_hello"}.

tools.name: list_characters
tools.description: Lists the cast in 3D: the six people (bob, ria, sunny, sam, lee, rose) and the animals (dog, cat, fox, horse, gull, and bear2, fox2, rabbit2, raccoon2, cat2 on two legs), each with the designed entry a cast entry gives it and a voice; the voices a line can use; and cartoon_example, a whole talking c

tools.name: get_move
tools.description: Returns one ready-made move: its block program as JSON, the same program as screenplay text, its length in seconds, what it works on, its settings with units, its page and links. Name it by id (c4c:beh:wave_hello), short name (wave_hello) or page slug. To write your own move, start from one, change

tools.name: validate
tools.description: Checks a cartoon, with the editor's own checks, before anyone sees it. Give one of cartoon, program, pack, character or file. Returns errors (it will not play as written: also a character or background the site lacks) and warnings, each {code, where, says, fix, url}, with did_you_mean and an RFC 690

tools.name: share_link
tools.description: Turns a cartoon, a scene, a move or a character into a jabbertoon.com link: it opens in the editor (a move in its move maker). It all travels after the #: nothing is uploaded or kept. All but a character's end with &from=ai (the page says an AI helper wrote it). One with errors gets them instead. Gi

tools.name: build
tools.description: Builds anything (a character, an animal, a car, a house) in Jabbertoon's 3D builder from steps, as its buttons do: spine, grow, bone (a skeleton, a bone at a time), add a ready part (leg, arm, head, wing, wheel, hat ...), set, copy, remove, look.
